title: Tenant graceful failover scenarios and evidence capture guide
content:
Purpose
This working guide collects realistic tenant-level failover scenarios for region-anchored customers and prescribes a lightweight, auditable evidence capture pattern operators should follow during drills and incidents. Target audience: oncall engineers, SRE operators for private deployments, solutions engineers who onboard sovereign customers, and compliance reviewers.

Context and motivation
We support tenants that are pinned to region-anchors (soft and hard pins). When we execute a graceful failover (planned maintenance, region outage, capacity migration), we need to: 1) ensure tenant traffic does not cross unauthorized jurisdictions, 2) meet SLA expectations and communicate clearly with customers, and 3) produce an auditable bundle that legal/compliance can use if asked. Current runbooks capture routing changes but lack consistent evidence payloads (what we captured, where it’s stored, TTL, and redaction guidance). This doc prescribes a minimal, operator-friendly standard.

Definitions (quick)
- Tenant: the customer logical account that may be region-anchored.
- Soft-pin: preference for a region but allowed fallback under constraints.
- Hard-pin: strict requirement; traffic must stay in-region except in documented emergency exceptions.
- Evidence bundle: a time-ordered artifact package (logs, config diffs, telemetry snapshots, decision notes) produced for each failover event.

When to produce a full evidence bundle
Produce full evidence for:
- Any hard-pin tenant failover (planned or unplanned)
- Soft-pin tenant failovers that crossed legal/regulatory boundaries or required approval (escalation to product/legal)
- Any incident marked P2+ that involved region-routing changes for multiple tenants

Evidence bundle contents (minimal required fields)
- incident-id: internal incident identifier (example: RES-2025-045)
- timeline.md: short narrative (what happened, why, who decided) — plain text summary, 5–12 bullets
- config-diff.jsonl: diffs of routing/pinning config before/after (redact secret keys)
- sample-traffic-headers.log: 50-200 anonymized request headers (hash tenant ids) showing region headers and X-Forwarded-For equivalents
- telemetry-snapshot.csv: token-level/distribution stats for window (see schema below)
- operator-commits.txt: list of commands and internal links (gitops commit IDs, orchestration actions)
- approval-record.txt: if approval required, a copy of the approver, timestamp and ticket id (redact personal email)

Storage and retention
Store evidence bundles in the dedicated residency-evidence bucket: s3://residency-evidence/{region}/{incident-id}/. Retention: 365 days by default for soft-pin events, 7 years for hard-pin customers (matches contracts). Access: legal and security groups have read-only access; operations must request time-limited tokens for downloads for audits.

Redaction policy
- Replace tenant_id and user identifiers with sha256 hashes and note the salt used in bundle-metadata (salt must be rotated per-month).
- Remove any PII in request bodies; if bodies must be retained for debugging, store a sanitized redacted copy and log a reason in timeline.md.
- Do NOT include full KMS keys or private keys; include key IDs only.

Telemetry snapshot schema (example CSV columns)
- timestamp, route, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, avg_latency_ms, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, error_rate, region, tenant_bucket
- Capture a 5–15 minute window around the event transition (start -2m to +10m).

Operator procedure (step-by-step)
Before the action (planned maintenance)
1) Create incident ticket (prefix RES) and link to tenant(s). Add expected window and rollback criteria.
2) Run preflight checks: capacity in target region, KV cache warming status, model compatibility matrix. Put output into config-diff.jsonl pre-state.
3) Notify CS and the customer (if SLA requires) with template message in communications/templates/residency-failover-notice.md.

During the action
1) Start a timeline.md entry noting the operator name, exact UTC start time, and the gitops commit used for routing change.
2) Execute change via automation where possible (invoke orchestration job id) and capture orchestration job URL and logs into operator-commits.txt.
3) Capture a sample of request headers for 5 minutes after the change (tool: telemetry-tool sample-headers --tenant <hashed> --limit 200 > sample-traffic-headers.log).
4) Dump telemetry snapshot (telemetry-cli snapshot --from <start-2m> --to <start+10m> --routes <affected> > telemetry-snapshot.csv).
5) If fallback triggered, log fallback reason code and approximate time in timeline.md and include config-diff post-state.

Unplanned failover (e.g., region outage) quick guidance
- Triage: declare incident, mark affected tenants with tag region-fallback. Prioritize hard-pin tenants for evidence bundling even if issue persists.
- If emergency traffic crosses boundary: stop and capture sampling immediately. Add note "boundary-crossing-detected" in timeline and escalate to legal (tag: legal-audit).

Minimal reproducible evidence examples (snippets)
- timeline.md example:
  - 2025-02-07T14:03:22Z: Operator L. Morgan started maintenance window (RES-2025-045).
  - 2025-02-07T14:05:07Z: Gitops commit abc123 applied: route-change tenant: <sha256(tenant)> -> region: eu-west-1 (soft pin fallback).
  - 2025-02-07T14:06:12Z: Telemetry spike p95 latency 2.1x baseline; fallback to warm pool triggered at 14:07:02Z.

- config-diff.jsonl example (single line diffs, redact token values):
  {"route":"tenant-<hash>","before":{"region":"us-west-2","pin_type":"soft"},"after":{"region":"eu-west-1","pin_type":"soft","reason":"planned-maintenance","gitops_commit":"abc123"}}

- sample-traffic-headers.log example (hash tenant ids):
  tenant_hash: e3b0c442..., region: eu-west-1, x-request-id: abcd-1234, geo-ip: 52.30.0.1

Checklist for compliance review (quick)
- [ ] incident ticket created and linked to evidence bundle path
- [ ] timeline.md contains decision rationale and approver(s) where required
- [ ] config-diff present and redacted correctly
- [ ] telemetry window captured and checked for boundary-crossing
- [ ] customer notification archived or template used
- [ ] evidence bundle uploaded to s3 path and retention tag set

Post-incident follow-ups
- Postmortem (postmortem template link) should include a section "Residency Evidence Audit" with reviewer signoff.
- For hard-pin customers, schedule a legal review to confirm evidence meets contractual obligations (tag a legal reviewer and upload sign-off).
- Drive follow-up action items into RESIDENCY-OPS backlog and mark owners.

Operational gotchas and tips
- Don’t rely on single-sample header captures. If automation fails, use low-level packet sampling as a backup (operator-only).
- For multi-tenant router changes, produce per-tenant evidence bundles; do not combine tenants into a single bundle for hard-pin customers.
- If you must keep request bodies for debugging, escalate to legal before retaining and ensure extra encryption-at-rest.

Open questions / items for next sprint
- Can we automate sample-headers capture into the orchestration job so evidence is produced automatically? (owner: Arjun)
- Proposal: add a registry of tenant retention policies with TTLs enforced by lifecycle rules (owner: Ben)
- Integrate with Redwood Console exports so CS can download customer-facing redacted bundles (owner: Sofia)

References and templates
- communications/templates/residency-failover-notice.md
- ops/templates/postmortem-residency-section.md
- CONFLUENCE-priv/residency-evidence-spec (source of truth for evidence object schema)
- JIRA-RESID-812 (work to add automated capture to orchestration)

Notes to reviewers
This is a working document — expecting feedback on the retention time defaults and the redaction salt pattern. If legal asks for stronger proofs (signed timestamps), we should add a step to notarize the bundle using our internal notarization service (TBD).

-- End of doc --
